tool_flagged.name: 2018 Subaru WRX STI
tool_flagged.reason: duplicate mesh (rule A): title token overlap 1.00 ignoring 'subaru', face counts 226,379 vs 227,058 (679 apart, 0.30%); keeping the higher face count
tool_flagged.eye_note: CONFIRMED. Both sheets audited individually at full resolution: two uploads of the same 2018 WRX STI VA facelift in white, 679 faces apart (0.30%). Identical bodywork, identical gloss-black alloy pattern, identical LED headlamp internals and honeycomb grille depth. Different uploaders (OUTPISTON vs Ddiaz Design), which is the usual re-upload signature. Keeping the 227,058-face copy.

reviewed_not_duplicates.eye_note: Three ZD8-generation BRZs, but the source titles state three different trims: bare BRZ (ZD8), 2024 BRZ tS and 2023 BRZ Premium. The tS carries a different rear wing, bumper and brake package in the renders. Per the no-fabricated-metadata rule the titles are the authority, so these stay as three entries.
Both ZC6-generation BRZ, but the titles state different years and trims (2013 BRZ vs 2020 BRZ tS) and the renders differ - the tS has the factory STI wing, bronze alloys and a facelift front bumper.

summary: dupe_check flagged 1 pair across 21 passes and it is CONFIRMED (1/1 precision on this wave). Its weakness here was recall, not precision: eyeballing all 21 passes found 4 further same-vehicle pairs it structurally cannot reach, because they are different meshes of the same car rather than re-uploads of one mesh. 21 passes -> 16 unique vehicles after 5 drops.
